- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is below recent high, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1) and forecast is above recent low, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 2% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and price is trending upward, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture mean reversion bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, forecast should not lag more than 1–2 days; adjust to align with recent trend.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to underestimate lows; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to avoid underestimating downside risk.
